message.content:
Here are some practical tips to keep your piano in top shape: | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |-----|----------------|--------------| | **Keep it at a stable humidity** | Pianos expand and contract with moisture changes, which can warp keys, soundboard, and action. | • Use a hygrometer inside the piano.
• Maintain 45‑55 % RH (relative humidity).
• In dry climates, use a humidifier; in damp areas, use a dehumidifier or silica gel packs. | | **Dust regularly** | Dust can clog the action and settle on the soundboard, affecting tone. | • Wipe down the lid, pedals, and exterior with a soft, dry cloth.
• Use a microfiber duster for the keys.
• Vacuum the inside of the lid with a brush attachment. | | **Avoid direct sunlight** | UV rays fade finish and can heat the piano unevenly. | • Keep the piano away from windows or use blinds/UV‑blocking curtains.
• If you must place it near a window, rotate it periodically. | | **Control temperature swings** | Rapid temperature changes can damage wood and affect tuning stability. | • Keep the room temperature between 65‑75 °F (18‑24 °C).
• Avoid placing the piano near radiators, vents, or heaters. | | **Use a piano cover when not in use** | Covers protect against dust, pets, and accidental knocks. | • Choose a breathable, non‑adhesive cover.
• Store it in a cool, dry place when not in use. | | **Check the tuning and action** | Even a well‑maintained piano will need periodic tuning and adjustments. | • Have a qualified technician tune it every 3–6 months.
• Ask them to inspect the action for sticking keys or loose hammers. | | **Keep it level** | An unlevel piano can develop uneven wear and affect tuning. | • Use a spirit level on the piano’s base.
• Adjust the legs or place shims under the feet as needed. | | **Avoid heavy objects on the lid** | Pressure can warp the lid and affect the soundboard. | • Never place books, cushions, or other items on the lid.
• Keep the lid closed when not playing. | | **Clean the pedals gently** | Pedal pads can accumulate grime and lose responsiveness. | • Wipe them with a damp cloth (no harsh chemicals).
• Replace worn pads every 1–2 years. | | **Schedule a yearly inspection** | A professional can spot hidden issues before they become costly. | • Arrange for a full inspection once a year.
• Discuss any concerns (e.g., cracks, water damage) with the technician. | ### Quick Checklist (Daily/Weekly) - [ ] Dust keys and exterior. - [ ] Check humidity level. - [ ] Ensure the piano is level. - [ ] Keep the lid closed when not playing. ### When to Call a Technician - Keys feel sticky or uneven. - Hammers don’t strike properly. - You hear buzzing or rattling sounds. - The piano has been exposed to water or extreme temperatures. - You notice cracks or warping. By following these habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s tone, extend its lifespan, and reduce the frequency of costly repairs. Happy playing!
